## What Is an Applicant Tracking System?


An applicant tracking system (ATS) manages hiring from start to finish, giving teams one place to post jobs, collect applications, and move candidates through each stage. SHRM describes the ATS as[the backbone of recruiting technology](https://www.shrm.org/mena/topics-tools/news/talent-acquisition/how-to-purchase-applicant-tracking-system) , storing resumes and automating job postings.


Core functions include:


-


Resume parsing and centralized candidate storage


-


Stage tracking from application through offer


-


Interview scheduling and automated candidate communications


-


Team collaboration and structured feedback collection


Hiring, even for one role, generates more information than any inbox can handle, so an ATS keeps candidates visible and organized. Nearly all[Fortune 500 companies use an ATS](https://careers.tufts.edu/resources/everything-you-need-to-know-about-applicant-tracking-systems-ats/) , and[research suggests 86% of recruiters](https://www.selectsoftwarereviews.com/blog/applicant-tracking-system-statistics) report reduced time-to-hire after implementing one.

Core features: job distribution, stage tracking, collaboration


-


Pricing transparency: clear upfront costs, usable free tiers


-


Integrations: job boards, HR tools, calendar apps


-


AI capabilities: resume scoring, outreach, interview assistance


-


Scalability: fits a 10-person startup or a 500-person org

## Best Overall Applicant Tracking System for Recruitment: Dover


[Dover’s free ATS](https://www.dover.com/ats) was built for founders and hiring managers who can’t spend weeks onboarding new software. Setup takes minutes, and the interface is familiar enough for anyone on your team to start tracking candidates right away.


Here’s what’s included at no cost:


-


A full ATS with unlimited jobs and users, candidate tracking, custom interview plans, and email templates


-


One-click distribution to 50+ job boards, including Indeed


-


A no-code careers page and referral tracking, with agency management on the Premium plan


AI applicant scoring and AI note taking sit on the $199/month Premium ATS plan instead of the free tier. See[AI-powered applicant tracking systems](https://www.dover.com/blog/ai-powered-applicant-tracking-systems) for how that scoring works.


Dover also offers an on-demand marketplace of vetted fractional recruiters who set their own rates, with[hires averaging about $4,800](https://www.dover.com/recruiters#cost-per-hire) instead of traditional agency placement fees. It is also the layer fractional recruiting agencies are built on, so agency teams and independent recruiters can run searches inside one ATS.


Dover works best for startups that want a full-featured ATS without monthly fees. Recruiters and hiring teams share one pipeline view, and every fractional recruiter in the marketplace carries real, verified client reviews.


## Workday


Workday is an enterprise HR suite built for large organizations managing complex workforce operations. Its ATS is bundled into an HCM system, covering recruiting, payroll, benefits, and workforce planning under one roof. For most small and mid-sized teams, though, Workday is overbuilt. Licensing costs are substantial, implementation can take months, and the configuration complexity often requires dedicated HR ops support to maintain. It tends to fit best when a company already runs Workday for HR and wants to avoid adding a separate recruiting tool to the mix.


## iCIMS


iCIMS Hire sits at the core of the iCIMS Talent Cloud and serves enterprise customers across technology, healthcare, finance, and manufacturing. It covers the full hiring lifecycle with applicant tracking, candidate relationship management, career site personalization, interview scheduling, and a recruitment marketing solution that distributes jobs across social networks and job boards, and the iCIMS Marketplace adds a marketplace of HR tool integrations on top of that. Pricing is typically quote-based and varies widely depending on company size, modules, and configuration.


Some users report the application flow can include many required steps before a candidate can submit. For high-volume enterprise recruiting, iCIMS is a capable system, though smaller teams that need a working ATS without complex setup will likely find it more than they need.


## Bullhorn


Bullhorn is built for staffing and recruitment agencies, covering sourcing, client placement, and payroll. Its combined ATS and CRM functionality lets recruiters see a candidate’s placement history alongside client contact notes in one record, so account managers and recruiters stay aligned without switching tools. AI-powered candidate-job matching, resume parsing, and client contact tracking sit within the same system.


Capterra and G2 user reviews often flag a dated interface, clunky candidate uploading, and integration headaches. Add-ons like email automation and LinkedIn integration often carry extra costs, and prices can increase at renewal depending on contract terms.


Bullhorn fits staffing agencies well. For companies focused on internal hiring, a fractional recruiting model built on a free ATS can often cover sourcing, screening, and offers with less added complexity.


## Jobvite


Jobvite covers end-to-end recruiting: candidate relationship management, recruitment marketing, applicant tracking, onboarding, and analytics. Its AI matching pairs candidates to roles based on skills and culture fit.


The catch is bundling. Jobvite is typically sold as a full suite, so some teams may end up paying for modules they do not use. Quote-based pricing can be a stretch for smaller teams.


Jobvite tends to fit mid-to-large enterprises running high-volume hiring that can use the full feature set. For startups that do not need recruitment marketing modules, a fractional recruiting model with a free ATS as the foundation can often cover sourcing and hiring with less overhead.


## Greenhouse


Greenhouse targets mid-to-large enterprises that need structured, customizable hiring workflows. Its reporting suite covers pipeline conversion rates, interview consistency, time-in-stage data, and diversity metrics. Greenhouse’s[partner directory lists hundreds of](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/) integrations, plus open API access, connecting it to most HR stacks. Pricing varies by company size and feature set, typically starting in the thousands per year, and growing teams often upgrade as needs expand. Greenhouse fits mid-to-large enterprises with the budget and admin time to configure it. Smaller teams hiring a handful of roles a year may find it more than they need.


## What’s Changing in ATS in 2026


The ATS market has shifted considerably as of October 2026. AI is no longer a differentiating feature. It’s a baseline expectation. Industry roundups suggest[most organizations](https://thecocogroup.com/best-applicant-tracking-systems-ats-in-2026-compared-ranked/) have now integrated AI or automation into their ATS workflow, so the key question has moved from whether a platform has AI to how good that AI is.


The better implementations in 2026 offer explainable candidate scoring (not opaque ranking), bias auditing, and AI-generated job descriptions. The weaker ones layer a chatbot on top of legacy infrastructure and call it intelligent recruiting.


A second shift: the ATS alone is increasingly not enough. Many recruiting teams now run several separate tools alongside their primary ATS, with point solutions for interview intelligence, skills assessment, and offer management filling gaps the core system leaves behind. For most startups, that means either picking an ATS that covers more natively, or keeping things lean with a free system and layering in only what’s needed.


An ATS handles the workflow of a search: posting jobs, tracking applicants, and moving candidates through stages. It typically doesn’t source passive candidates, run intake calls, or close offers. When a role is senior or specialized, inbound applications run thin, or the internal team lacks recruiting bandwidth, a fractional recruiter or fractional recruiting agency can add that capacity on top of the existing ATS. As a rule of thumb, fractional support often fits teams making roughly 5 to 50 hires a year, while a first full-time recruiter often starts to make sense around 15 to 20 annual hires, with the two ranges overlapping depending on role complexity. This tends to work best when the recruiter and the hiring team share one ATS, so both sides can see pipeline status and stage tracking in real time. Dover is one example of this approach: a free ATS that fractional recruiting agencies build on, paired with a marketplace of fractional recruiters who carry real, vetted reviews.


## Why Dover Is the Best Applicant Tracking System for Recruitment


The free ATS, with unlimited jobs and users and no per-seat fees, handles the pipeline: job posts, candidate tracking, and stage visibility. Fractional recruiters plug in on top inside that same ATS when a search needs sourcing, screening, or closing help, so both sides see candidate flow in real time.


Hires through the marketplace average about $4,800 instead of placement fees that scale with salary, with no long-term contracts. For startups and small businesses hiring without a dedicated recruiting team, that combination can be a fit worth considering.


## FAQs


### What’s the difference between a free ATS and paid enterprise systems like Greenhouse or Workday?


Free systems like Dover cover core applicant tracking, job posting, candidate screening, and team collaboration without per-seat fees. Paid enterprise platforms add custom workflows, deeper reporting, and hundreds of integrations, but they often come with implementation timelines of weeks or months and quote-based pricing that commonly starts in the thousands of dollars per year. For many small teams, that gap may not support the added cost.


### Do I need a recruiter if I’m already using an ATS?


An ATS manages the workflow of hiring: collecting applications, tracking candidates through stages, and scheduling interviews. It typically doesn’t source, screen, or close candidates who aren’t already applying. When inbound volume is solid and a team has bandwidth, an ATS alone can often carry the process. For senior, specialized, or thin-pipeline roles, a fractional recruiter can add capacity inside the existing ATS, so pipeline notes and stage tracking stay in one shared system. With Dover, that means a free ATS paired with on-demand recruiters, with hires through the marketplace averaging about $4,800.


### What ATS tools work best for YC startups and early-stage companies?


Early-stage companies tend to need tools that work immediately, don’t require a dedicated HR team, and don’t lock them into annual contracts. Dover fits that profile: the ATS is free with no seat limits, setup takes minutes, and vetted recruiters are available when a role gets competitive. At that stage, the overhead of enterprise systems like Workday or Greenhouse often doesn’t make sense.


## Final Thoughts on Selecting Your Recruiting ATS


Dover is one example of how that balance can work: a free ATS that fractional recruiting agencies and fractional recruiters build on, with real reviews of each recruiter, hires averaging about $4,800, and no long-term contract.
